title: Recovering Population Laws and Causal Queries from Two Cohorts with Complementary Selection
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded subfield below the field floor: paper-score ceiling 6.7 < 7.4; salvageable false.
gap_reasons: The all-ADMG statement is nevertheless an exact-source-design reduction built from classical positive matrix scaling, not a characterization of multi-source recovery with overlapping selector blocks, zeros, or general kernel releases.

The front-door boundary is sharp only within the specified menu of raw source margins and exact selector-parent restrictions, while the opposite selector enlargement yields a complete result only for one binary intervention-risk coordinate.

The absence of finite-sample inference, an applied design analysis, or evidence that the release savings matter materially in realistic studies limits the completed package's significance at a leading econometrics journal.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved an all-finite-ADMG complementary-block selected-source recovery theorem and a front-door release-menu boundary with positive separating witnesses. Pearl's front-door result was verified at Theorem 2/equation (9), and the worked witness arithmetic was adjudicated as F_PT=53/120 versus F_P=17/40. The final reviewer graded the contribution subfield, below the field floor (6.7 versus 7.4), and found no bounded same-topic repair; the math panel also recorded one missing graph dependency and two ballast illustration nodes for any future reuse.
tldr: For any finite ADMG, a full cohort law selected only by a variable block \(\mathbf Z\), together with the separate \(\mathbf X\)- and \(\mathbf Z\)-margins of a second cohort selected only by a disjoint block \(\mathbf X\), uniquely recovers the population observational law by positive diagonal scaling. A causal query is therefore identifiable from these releases exactly when it is ordinarily identifiable from the recovered law, with nonidentification transferred by observational-equivalence witnesses. The front-door specialization identifies the entire intervention law without the auxiliary joint table; its front-door-specific release-menu theorem proves uniform marginal-menu minimality with positive SCM twins, and the outcome-selector enlargement yields the sharp observable convex-hull region.
gap: Graphical recovery algorithms address selected data sources, and classical compatibility and scaling results reconstruct joint tables, but the inspected literature does not state which marginal releases are exactly necessary for a front-door intervention law or the observable sharp hull under treatment-contaminated outcome selection.
fill: The project supplies a finite-alphabet release iff with positive latent-SCM necessity witnesses, a reproducible binary certificate, and an analytic outcome-selector convex hull; the opposite selector enlargement appears only as a diagnostic boundary case.
